newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bourse says trading halted for rest of day.
newsitem.headline: Thai bourse says trading halted for rest of day.

text.p: Thailand's stock exchange said on Monday that there would be no trading on the market for the rest of the day after a series of false starts due to computer problems.

The market opened for a few minutes before the computer failed. The exchange then said trading would resume at 0445 GMT but that too failed to materialise. When the afternoon session resumed, as had been promised by the exchange, the computer again almost immediately failed to execute trading between brokerages and the bourse, brokers said.
When trading started briefly in the afteronoon, the SET Index had dropped 9.50 points, or 1.63 percent, to 571.63 by 0732 GMT. The SET 50 fell 1.03 points, or 2.42 percent to 41.46.
"The computer failure is beyond our control. But we are confident that the trading would resume as normal tomorrow," the SET spokesman Suvicha Mingkwan told reporters.
This is the first time since the exchange introduced electronic and scripless trading since 1991 that it has had such a major computer failure and trading has been halted for the whole day.
